name: manual_e8a561
claim: Before removing a config-writing function, grep every consumer of the values it writes across the whole codebase (not just the obvious module) to confirm nothing reads them back — dead-write code can look load-bearing.

decisions.notes: discover.py wrote live LAN IPs into Perpetua-Tools' git-tracked config/devices.yml and config/models.yml on every startup, dirtying the repo with ephemeral DHCP topology and risking a doxxing leak via git add -A. Grepping orchestrator/ and src/perpetua/ for the lan_ip field showed zero Python readers — it was pure write-only dead metadata; the models.yml host default was consulted only as a last-resort fallback when an env var was unset, and that env var was already kept live from an untracked discovery snapshot. Verifying zero readers first made it safe to delete the writer outright instead of just gating or documenting it.
